analysis.title: Global Fixed Income Strategy, November/December 2026
key_insights: French bonds had a record sell-off in October. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread passed 170 basis points on Oct 22 and has since retreated. The 2-year spread hit 87 bps before falling to about 58 bps. Five-year euro swap rates are up 80-90 bps year-to-date.
Invesco blames a structural fiscal problem that has become acute, not a single shock. France's primary deficit is about 3% of GDP, while some eurozone countries now run primary surpluses.

Stabilizing French debt at 100% of GDP would need about 4% of GDP in fiscal consolidation, a swing from a near 3% primary deficit to a 1% primary surplus. Net interest burden could rise from 2.6% of GDP in 2026 toward 5% by 2035.

French politics offers no clear path to consolidation. Spring 2027 presidential elections and summer parliamentary elections add uncertainty. Marine Le Pen leads the polls, but her plan relies on EUR9B of EU budget cuts and EUR6B of fraud savings rather than spending reform.

Eurozone inflation is forecast to peak above 4%, revised up from the mid-3%s on gas prices. Invesco expects the ECB deposit rate to rise to 2.75% in December. If the ECB hikes to 2.75-3%, it may need to cut next year.

The ECB's TPI and OMT tools require a 'sustainable fiscal path', which France does not meet. Invesco separates a France-specific repricing, which the ECB may tolerate, from broader fragmentation, which would likely trigger a policy response.
Moody's left France's rating unchanged on Oct 23. Invesco would treat a 250-300 bps OAT-Bund spread as dire. It notes France is AA rated and 'not Greece'.

Credit dispersion has returned. US credit is outperforming Europe, IG is beating HY, BBs are beating CCCs, and tech is lagging non-tech. The catalyst is rates: the 10-year UST briefly passed 5%, the 30-year hit its highest yield since 2004, and the MOVE index rose from 75 to 100 between Aug 31 and Nov 2.
US IG is described as the steadiest part of credit. The Bloomberg US Credit index yields near 6%, and spreads have recently widened beyond this year's tight range.

The BB-BBB spread differential widened to about 89 bps (BB OAS 203 vs BBB 114), near twelve-month wides. The CCC index yields nearly 16%, with spreads above 1,000 bps near 10-year wides. Invesco sees no broad default cycle and favors higher-quality BBs.

US IG tech trades about 25 bps wide of the broad IG index, versus a 20-year median of about 15 bps inside it. Drivers are record hyperscaler supply and questions over AI payback on more than USD3 trillion of expected capex through 2029. 2027 supply is likely to top 2026. Invesco favors selective, structured hyperscaler credit.

European IG is near its widest versus US IG in 12 months. Invesco is more constructive on European IG, sees value in select European financials, and sees cross-currency value where euro bonds trade cheap to dollar bonds from the same issuer.

US rates: overweight. The sell-off reflects resilient growth, not inflation. The Fed skipped in October despite an upside inflation surprise, December is live, and the lack of forward guidance under Chair Warsh keeps front-end volatility high. 30-year TIPS are near 3.40%, 10-year TIPS near 3%, and 2-year yields near 5%. Long-end shorts are extreme. Invesco expects the belly to outperform.

Europe rates: neutral. The ECB held in October and December is live. Limited scope to price out hikes with energy rising. Fiscal support and defense spending likely raise long-end risk premia, so Invesco expects a steeper curve.

China rates: downgraded to neutral. The PBOC now uses the overnight reverse repo rate as its key benchmark and has set up the Bond Market NBFI Swap Facility. 2027 infrastructure funding needs and limited outperformance vs developed markets drove the downgrade.

Japan rates: neutral. JGB yields fell with Treasuries and the late-October 20-year auction had a record bid-to-cover. The BoJ says 2% inflation is achieved, and quarterly hikes to a 2% terminal rate look like the base case. Invesco expects further curve flattening beyond 10 years from repatriation demand.

UK rates: overweight, favoring shorter maturities. The BoE is very likely to hike 25 bps in November. Markets price over 100 bps of hikes, and Invesco sees the extra 40 bps priced vs the Fed and ECB as unwarranted. Gilts have underperformed Treasuries and Bunds.

Australia rates: overweight. Yields are down about 25 bps from the early October peak. Invesco expects the RBA to hike to 4.85% in November as the last of the cycle, sees long-term yields above 5% as good value, and prefers long-term forwards to 10-year bonds.

FX: neutral USD. Underweight EUR (weak growth, energy, French stress) and GBP (trade-weighted index near record highs, BoE unlikely to validate hike pricing). Overweight CNY, JPY and AUD. Yen longs are best expressed against the euro.

The PBOC raised financial institutions' FX reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6% on Nov 3. Invesco reads this as an attempt to slow renminbi appreciation, but expects further gains after consolidation.

Municipals: the Bloomberg Municipal Bond Index fell 4.36% in September, then returned 3.85% in October, its best October on record. Invesco says rates, not credit, drove both moves. Tax-equivalent yield-to-worst hit 9.89% on Sept 29, the highest since Oct 2008. Invesco still sees value in longer maturities and a steep muni curve.

sector_views.rationale: Large balance sheets, strong liquidity and long maturity runways help it absorb higher rates better than levered credits.
Spreads are at record relative wides, but record hyperscaler supply and AI capex payback questions mean Invesco wants only selective, well-structured exposure.
BBs now pay more for a modest step down from BBB, and Invesco sees no broad default cycle.
CCCs yield nearly 16% with spreads above 1,000 bps. Levered structures have less room to absorb higher financing costs.
Sovereign stress has pushed it near 12-month wides versus US IG, with value in select financials and cross-currency pairs.
September's sell-off was rate-driven, credit fundamentals are solid, tax-equivalent yields are high, and longer maturities lag the rally.

tension_points.bull_case: The ECB may tolerate a France-specific repricing. Moody's left the rating unchanged, France is AA rated, and pooled European debt facilities link member states' fates.
tension_points.bear_case: France cannot meet the fiscal path conditions for TPI and OMT, there is no clear political leader for consolidation, and the market may not yet price the full problem.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An OAT-Bund spread of 250-300 bps, or broader fragmentation that threatens monetary transmission.

tension_points.bull_case: Real yields are high, 2-year yields near 5% offer carry, and long-end shorts are extreme.
tension_points.bear_case: Resilient growth, fiscal sustainability and geopolitical risk could push long-end yields higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth data, consumption in particular, staying strong rather than softening.
